plan.contextChunk: This figure shows a uniform thin disk twice, in two side-by-side views. The left view looks straight down the rotation axis: a blue-shaded circle with x pointing up, y pointing right, and z labeled at the center where the axis emerges from the page. A double-headed arrow from center to outer edge is labeled R, a second arrow labeled r reaches a thin orange ring concentric with the rim, and a short arrow labeled dr points at that ring's width. The right view redraws the disk in oblique perspective as a shaded ellipse with an orange rim, z vertical, y to the right, x coming toward the lower left; a curved arrow loops around z to show the sense of rotation, and an arrow labeled r runs from the center to an element on the ring labeled dm. Showing the ring face-on and in perspective ties the annular strip of width dr to the mass element dm at one distance from the axis. The pairing motivates finding the moment of inertia by summing thin rings, each carrying all its mass at radius r.

interactionPlan.concept: The moment of inertia of a uniform disk is found by slicing it into thin concentric rings of radius r and width dr, each ring carrying all its mass dm at one distance from the rotation axis, and summing their r²·dm contributions.
elements: face-on view (left): blue-shaded circular disk with center origin
face-on axes: x pointing up, y pointing right, z labeled at center (axis out of page)
orange annular ring of radius r and width dr, concentric with the disk
double-headed arrow labeled R from center to outer rim
arrow labeled r from center to the orange ring
short arrow labeled dr indicating the ring's thickness
perspective view (right): blue-shaded ellipse (tilted disk) with orange rim
perspective axes: z vertical, y to the right, x toward the lower left
curved rotation arrow looping around the z axis
arrow labeled r from center to a mass element on the ring
small highlighted mass element labeled dm on the ring
contribution indicator showing r²·dm growing with r

interactions.label: Ring radius r
interactions.teaches: A ring's contribution to moment of inertia grows as r² — mass farther from the axis counts disproportionately more, which is why the disk's I is less than if all mass sat at the rim

interactions.label: Ring width dr
interactions.teaches: The ring's mass dm is proportional to its area 2πr·dr — the differential strip supplies the mass element being summed in the integral

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The same annular integration element appears as a concentric ring face-on and as a tilted band around the rotation axis in perspective — it is one full ring at a single radius r, not a patch

demo_steps.title: Slice the disk into rings
demo_steps.narration: The disk is decomposed into thin concentric rings. The highlighted orange ring sits at radius r with thickness dr — every bit of its mass is the same distance from the axis.

demo_steps.title: Move the ring outward
demo_steps.narration: Drag r toward the rim: the ring's r²·dm contribution indicator grows quadratically. Mass near the edge contributes far more to the moment of inertia than the same mass near the center.

demo_steps.title: Widen the strip
demo_steps.narration: Increase dr and watch the shaded strip area — and hence dm — grow. In the limit dr → 0 the ring becomes the differential mass element dm = (2M/R²) r dr inside the integral.

demo_steps.title: See it in perspective
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the tilted view: the same ring wraps around the vertical z axis as the disk spins, and the dm marker rides the ring — confirming the integration element is a full annulus at one radius.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Because every point of a thin ring is the same distance r from the axis, its moment of inertia is simply r²dm — summing these ring contributions from r=0 to r=R yields the disk's I = ½MR².
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two side-by-side panels sharing one highlighted annulus. Left panel: flat blue-lavender filled circle, black axes (x up, y right), 'z' labeled at the center dot, orange ring of adjustable radius and thickness, arrows labeled R (to rim), r (to ring), dr (ring thickness). Right panel: same disk drawn as a flattened ellipse in oblique view with orange rim, z axis vertical with a curved rotation arrow around it, y to the right, x angled down-left, a small dark mass element labeled dm sitting on the ring with an r arrow from center to it. Use a warm orange for the ring in both views and keep the two views synchronized: changing r or dr updates both panels simultaneously. Add a small readout near the ring showing dm and r²·dm values updating with the sliders.

authoredContext:
Integrating to find the moment of inertia of a two-dimensional object is a little bit trickier, but one shape is commonly done at this level of study—a uniform thin disk about an axis through its center (the figure).

Calculating the moment of inertia for a thin disk about an axis through its center.

Figure shows a uniform thin disk of radius r that rotates about a Z axis that passes through its center.

Since the disk is thin, we can take the mass as distributed entirely in the xy-plane. We again start with the relationship for the surface mass density, which is the mass per unit surface area. Since it is uniform, the surface mass density σ is constant:

discrepancies: the 'r' label in the perspective (right) panel is missing: refresh() calls lblPosR.remove() immediately after rebuildRight() creates it, so only the bare double-headed arrow and 'dm' remain, whereas the source clearly labels 'r' in the perspective view

in the source the face-on 'dr' arrow points across the orange band at the upper-right rim; the generated dr arrow floats well outside the band and points at empty space near the rim, weakening the radial-thickness reading

the perspective disk's outer rim is stroked in orange in the generated figure, but in the source the orange/red ring is the inner annulus element while the outer rim reads as the disk edge — the generated figure makes the rim itself look like the highlighted element

source face-on panel labels the horizontal axis to the right as 'y' and vertical as 'x' (unusual but intentional); generated matches this, but the added readout text and contribution bar below the panels are extra elements not in the source
evaluation.notes: Both panels (face-on ring with R/r/dr and tilted spinning disk with z-axis rotation arrow and dm) are recognizably reproduced, and the r/dr sliders, perspective toggle, and 4-step demo are all functional and pedagogically apt; the main flaw is the accidentally deleted 'r' label in the perspective panel and a dr arrow that doesn't sit on the band.
action_items: Fix the label leak in refresh()/rebuildRight(): rebuildRight creates a new 'r' label each call without removing the previous one, and refresh then removes the just-created label — track and remove the old label before creating the new one so exactly one visible 'r' label remains in the perspective panel.
Reposition the face-on dr arrow so it straddles the orange band radially (arrowheads at radii r and r+dr along the same ray) instead of floating outside the rim.
Remove or restyle the orange stroke on the perspective disk's outer rim so the highlighted annulus (inner orange ellipse) is the only orange element, matching the source.
